name: DataGrid
intent: An editable table: people click a cell to add or change its content, like rule conditions, line items or mappings.
usage: Use DataGrid when people enter or change data in rows, not just read it. It is one component: pass columns and rows as data. Each column has a type: text and number cells edit in place with a kit Input, select cells are a kit Select, formula cells open a kit FormulaEditor in the cell, date cells are a kit DatePicker, and readOnly columns only show. Click a cell or press Enter to edit; Enter or leaving the cell saves, Escape cancels, Tab moves to the next cell. rowNumbers adds a # column. canAddRows adds an Add row button under the grid; canInsertRows, canRemoveRows and canDeleteRows each add a button to the action column at the end of every row, in that order: + adds an empty row under this one, X takes the row out of this grid, and the trash deletes the record everywhere it is used. Two stand on the row and any after that go in a More menu at the end, so with all three on, Delete is in the menu. Keep remove and delete apart: a row people only meant to take off a quote is removed, not deleted. Delete asks first in a kit AlertDialog and only then calls onDeleteRow. actionsFor picks, row by row, which of those a row shows, so a saved row can carry the trash and a row added since the X. selectable adds a checkbox column at the start, with select-all in the header, for actions on several rows at once. Columns are at least 160 wide unless they hug. The first column (and #) stays pinned when the grid scrolls sideways. setForAll on a column adds a Set for all menu under its title. detail makes rows expandable, with settings or sub-rows under each row. Inside a Form with columns, the grid spans the row, and with start labels it starts at the section's edge, since its column headers stand in for a label. For read-only lists use Table. See contracts/datagrid.json for the full contract.

columns.itemShape: { key: string; header: string; type?: "text" | "number" | "select" | "formula" | "date"; options?: SelectOption[]; searchable?: boolean; searchPlaceholder?: string; placeholder?: string; readOnly?: boolean; hug?: boolean; width?: string; fields?: FormulaField[]; onCalculate?: (formula: string) => string; setForAll?: boolean; opensDetail?: boolean }
columns.note: type defaults to text. options for select. date cells are always a kit DatePicker (size sm); their value is an ISO date, YYYY-MM-DD, shown formatted, and placeholder fills the empty field. A readOnly date column has no picker: it writes the same formatted date as plain text in the row's own font, so a column people cannot change does not read as code. fields and onCalculate for formula, passed to the FormulaEditor. hug makes the column only as wide as its content; otherwise it is at least 160 wide. width is a CSS width. searchable adds a search field at the top of a select column's list that filters options by label, for long lists like a product catalog; searchPlaceholder names it (default Search). setForAll adds a Set for all menu under the column title: Use row 1 value copies the first row's value to every row, Clear all rows empties the column. opensDetail (on a readOnly column, with detail and detailCount) puts a kit Button holding a Count of the other values after the cell's value that opens and closes the row's detail, and the grid drops its toggle column. The open detail lines up under that column (at least --data-grid-detail-min wide, 360px) and slides back toward the start when it would run past the grid's visible edge: use it when the cell shows the first of several values, like the first rate band.

rows.note: Controlled rows, one value per column key.

defaultRows.note: Starting rows when rows is not controlled.

onRowsChange.note: (rows: DataGridRow[]) => void. Runs when a cell is saved and when rows are added or removed.

size.note: Row height 38 / 40 (editable cells keep 8px padding; Table is 36 / 40), header 40. Without a size it is md. A surrounding Density changes these sizes through the density tokens (Default values shown). Formula cells grow while they are edited.

line.note: The line under the header row: medium is 2px, thin is 1px. Every header takes it, with or without Set for all.

rowNumbers.note: A # column with each row's number.

canAddRows.note: An Add row button under the grid. The new row starts empty and its first cell opens for editing.

canRemoveRows.note: An X button in the action column, named Remove row 2 by a kit Tooltip. It takes the row out of this grid only; nothing else in the app changes. For a row that holds a saved record, pair it with canDeleteRows.

canDeleteRows.note: A trash button in the action column, named Delete row 2 by a kit Tooltip. It is the destructive one: the row goes, and so does the record behind it, everywhere in the app. It asks first in a kit AlertDialog — the grid owns that — and only on Delete does the row go and onDeleteRow run. With insert and remove also on it is the action that moves into the More menu.

onDeleteRow.note: (row: DataGridRow) => void. Runs once the person confirms the delete, with the row that went, so the screen can delete the record itself. onRowsChange runs too, with the row gone. Nothing runs if they cancel.

deleteConfirm.note: (row: DataGridRow) => { title: string; description: string }. What the delete confirmation says. Without it the title names the row by its first column (Delete API calls (per 10K)?, or Delete row 2? when that cell is empty) and the description says the record goes everywhere and cannot be brought back. Pass it to name the kind of record, like Delete usage identifier?

canInsertRows.note: A + button in the action column at the end of each row that adds an empty row just under it. Named by a kit Tooltip, like Add row below row 2.

actionsFor.note: (row: DataGridRow) => ("insert" | "remove" | "delete")[]. Which of the actions the grid turns on this row shows, like the trash on a row that holds a saved record and the X on a row added since. Without it every row shows them all.

selectable.note: Adds a checkbox column at the start, with a select-all in the header, for acting on several rows at once (like Add pricing on the ticked rates). It is pinned with the first column.

selected.note: Controlled ids of the ticked rows.

defaultSelected.note: Starting ticks when selected is not controlled.

onSelectionChange.note: (ids: string[]) => void. Select all ticks every row in the grid; clearing it unticks only them, so ticks on rows a filter hides stay.

rowLabel.note: Column key whose value names each row checkbox, like Select Gold plan. Defaults to the first column.

emptyLabel.note: Shown across the columns when there are no rows.

label.note: Names the grid for screen readers, and each cell's field, like Value, row 2.

stickyFirstColumn.note: The # column and the first column stay in place while the grid scrolls sideways; their end border is the same thin line as every cell. Put the column that names each row first.

detail.note: (row: DataGridRow) => ReactNode. Makes rows expandable: a toggle column comes first, and an open row shows this under it in one cell across the grid, kept to the grid's visible width. Return null for a row with nothing to show: it gets no toggle and cannot open, so the toggle itself says the row has more, like rate tiers. Put kit pieces in it: a Form of settings, a nested DataGrid (size sm) for sub-rows people edit like rate bands, or a Table (size sm) for sub-rows they only read. The grid's own cell look stays on its own cells, so a Table inside keeps the Table look.

detailCount.note: (row: DataGridRow) => number | undefined. With an opensDetail column: how many more values the row's detail holds, shown as a Count in the cell's button. A row with no number (or a null detail) gets no button and cannot open.

expanded.note: Controlled: ids of the rows whose detail is open.

defaultExpanded.note: Starting open rows when expanded is not controlled.

onExpandedChange.note: (ids: string[]) => void. Runs when a row opens or closes.

rowParent.note: (row: DataGridRow) => string | undefined. Groups rows: a row whose rowParent returns another row's id sits under that row, one step in. The parent shows a square toggle (indeterminate_check_box open, add_box shut) at the start of its first cell that hides and shows its rows, and the first column's header holds one toggle for every group. Keep a group's rows right after their parent in rows.

collapsed.note: Controlled ids of the parent rows whose rows are hidden.

defaultCollapsed.note: Starting shut groups when collapsed is not controlled.

onCollapsedChange.note: (ids: string[]) => void. Runs when a group opens or shuts, or the header toggle does them all.

cellStatus.itemShape: (row: DataGridRow, key: string) => { intent: "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "info" | "neutral"; label: string; icon?: string; tint?: boolean } | undefined
cellStatus.note: A filled status icon after the cell's value, like posted (success, check_circle) or not posted (warning, remove_circle); icon overrides the intent's glyph and label names it for screen readers. tint fills the cell with the intent's faint background (bg-*-faint), like months not posted yet. Return undefined for a plain cell.

cellReadOnly.note: (row: DataGridRow, key: string) => boolean. Read only cell by cell, on top of a column's readOnly: a schedule's product rows only show, while their adjustment rows edit.

cellLink.note: (row: DataGridRow, key: string) => boolean. Draws the cell's value as a link. On a read-only cell it is a kit Link that calls onCellLink; on a cell that edits, the value is underlined in the brand colour and clicking it opens the editor as usual.

onCellLink.note: (row: DataGridRow, key: string) => void. Runs when a read-only link cell is clicked, like a product name opening its record.

totalRow.note: A row at the bottom that adds the others up, like Period total: read only, on bg-neutral-subtle, medium weight. Its value per column key; it is never selectable, grouped or given actions.

legend.note: A key under the grid to the cellStatus icons, like Posted and Unposted: each item is the same filled icon, then its name.

useWhen: People build or change rows of data in place: rule conditions, price tiers, field mappings, line items.
Short editable lists where a form per row would be slow.
doNot: Do not use it to show data people only read. Use Table.
Do not invent an EditableCell, GridRow or a table of loose inputs. Pass columns with a type.
Do not put loose checkboxes beside the grid to pick rows. Pass selectable.
Do not build your own expand arrows or a second table under a row. Pass detail.
Do not put a Form around each row. Save the rows from onRowsChange.
Do not use the trash for a row people are only taking off this grid. X removes, the trash deletes the record for everyone.
Do not ask again before a delete from the screen. The grid already shows the AlertDialog; onDeleteRow runs after it.
a11y: A native table named by label, with kit HeaderCell headers.

Each editable cell is a button named by its column and row with its value, like Value, row 2: 100. Enter or click opens a kit Input, Select or FormulaEditor named the same way, and focus moves into it.
Enter saves and Escape cancels; focus goes back to the cell. Tab moves to the next cell.

The action column at the end of a row holds up to two buttons in reading order — Add row below row 2, Remove row 2, Delete row 2 — each a kit Button named that way, with the same words in a kit Tooltip. Any past the first two go in a kit Dropdown named More actions, row 2, with Delete marked danger.
Set for all is a kit Dropdown under the column title; the header is still the kit HeaderCell.

With detail, each row that has one starts with a kit Button named Show details, row 2 (Hide when open), with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at the open detail, a group named Details, row 2. A row whose detail is null has no button.
A date cell is a kit DatePicker named by its column and row, like Start date, row 2.
With an opensDetail column, the Count button is named N more, row 2, with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at the open detail.
Delete opens a kit AlertDialog: it holds focus until the person cancels or confirms, and Cancel has focus first.

With selectable, each row starts with a kit Checkbox named Select and the row's first value (or rowLabel's), like Select Gold plan, and the header holds a select-all kit HeaderCell checkbox that reads mixed when only some rows are ticked. Ticked rows carry aria-selected.
snippet:
<DataGrid
  label="Conditions"
  columns={[
    { key: "field", header: "Field", type: "formula", fields: accountFields },
    { key: "condition", header: "Condition", type: "select", options: conditions, width: "200px" },
    { key: "value", header: "Value" },
  ]}
  rows={rules}
  onRowsChange={setRules}
  canAddRows
  canRemoveRows
/>

examples.title: Conditions
examples.usage: Field is a formula cell, Condition a Select and Value text. Click a cell to edit it; add and remove rows.

examples.title: Line items
examples.usage: number cells align to the end. A readOnly column shows values people cannot change — Billed from is a readOnly date, so it reads as the kit writes a date rather than as the day it is stored as. Small size for denser rows. Quantity has Set for all under its title.

examples.title: Dates and details
examples.usage: Start and End are date cells. API calls opens to its rate bands, a nested grid with a Currency select, and starts open. Seat license has one price, so its detail is null and it has no toggle. All three row actions are on, so the column at the end holds + and X, and Delete sits in the More menu: + adds a row under this one, X takes the row off this subscription, and Delete asks first, then takes the product out of the app.

examples.title: Pick rows
examples.usage: A bulk edit: tick rows to act on them together. Saved rows carry the trash; a row added since carries the X.

examples.title: More values in a cell
examples.usage: Tiered rates. Rate is a readOnly opensDetail column: Sandbox Environment shows its first band, USD 0–10,000: 1,800.00, then a Count button with 2, the number of other bands. It opens the row to every band in a read-only Table size sm, line thin, captioned Sandbox Environment: 3 rates in USD. Seat license has one price, so its detail is null: no button, and no toggle column.

examples.title: Empty
examples.usage: No rows yet: headers stay, and Add row starts the first one.

examples.title: Revenue schedule
examples.usage: A schedule grouped by product. Each product row (read only, its name a link) has its Manual adjustments row under it, opened and shut by the square toggle; the header's toggle does every group. January to March carry a green posted mark; later months an orange unposted mark on a faint warning fill. Adjustments edit in place and read as links (-- when empty). Period total sits at the bottom, and the key under the grid names the two marks.
